summary.prose: The authoring stages learn one way to write a file reference and the artifact check enforces its shape. A project file is written relative to the project root, with an optional line number, on its own and with no prose beside it; a file outside the project is written with its full path. The rule is defined once and placed in the prompts and the schema descriptions of the fields that carry paths, and a new check refuses an artifact whose call sites or code and doc citations are not in that form, so the model is told which entries to fix and re-emits. Existing records are not rewritten.

dataModelChanges.details: The kind union gains 'paths', next to 'schema' | 'citations' | 'boundary'. No consumer switches exhaustively on it. The daemon's correction loop only tests for 'boundary', so a 'paths' failure takes the same plain re-emit as a citations failure. The in-session phase (the one controllers use through insrc_workflow_step) builds the error code from the kind, so a path failure comes back as a retryable 'synthesize-paths' error with the offending entries in its message, and the controller re-emits.

The bare string-array schemas for callSites and pathsCited gain a description that carries the shared rule wording, and the synthesize prompts that emit citations carry the rule itself; no pattern is added to the schema, because a violation is reported by the check with the entries named, not by a generic schema error. The design.story synthesize prompt's 'verbatim from s4' hard rule gets the one stated exception for call sites.

errorCases.scenario: A call site or a code or doc citation ref carries prose beside the path, for example 'src/workflow/artifacts/plan.ts (new artifact module)'.
errorCases.detection: checkPathForms finds whitespace or a character outside a path in the entry and adds it to the failure details.
errorCases.response: validateBodyAndCitations returns a 'paths' failure naming the entry; the synthesize turn is re-emitted with the entries listed. A call site that came from the s4 step is corrected in the re-emit, because the rule in the synthesize prompt lets the synthesizer write it in the path form instead of copying s4 verbatim.
errorCases.userImpact: None once re-emitted; the artifact is not written until every entry is a path.

errorCases.scenario: A model keeps emitting a bad path on every re-emit.
errorCases.detection: The retry limit that bounds a citations failure is reached (the daemon-side loop), or, in a controller-driven run, the controller stops re-emitting; the in-session error stays retryable.
errorCases.response: The synthesize turn fails with the 'paths' failure and its details, as a citations failure does today.
errorCases.userImpact: The stage reports the entries that were refused instead of writing a record with references that do nothing.

errorCases.scenario: A well-formed project path that is shortened, such as artifacts/plan.ts, is emitted.
errorCases.detection: Not detected: the check reads only the string and cannot tell a shortened path from a path to another directory.

migration.stateBefore: The path-valued fields (dataModel[].callSites, the analyze-bundle pathsCited, and the ref of a code or doc citation) are bare strings. Nothing states the form of a path to the model and validateBodyAndCitations checks only boundary rules and citation grounding, so a shortened path or a path with prose beside it is written as it is emitted (search.text and file reads of src/workflow/synthesizer.ts, src/workflow/runners/design-story/schemas.ts and src/workflow/artifacts/lld.ts in s1).
migration.stateAfter: The shared rule PATH_FORM_RULE sits in every synthesize prompt and in the step prompts and schema field descriptions that author paths, and validateBodyAndCitations also runs checkPathForms on call sites and on the refs of code and doc citations, returning a 'paths' failure that names the entries to fix. Records already written are not changed or re-checked.

migrationSteps.action: Add PATH_FORM_RULE to the shared prompt fragments module and describe the path-valued schema fields with it.
Add the 'paths' kind to the validation failure and the path check, and call it from validateBodyAndCitations after the boundary and citation checks.

Interpolate the rule into every synthesize prompt in src/workflow/orchestrator.ts (stub, brainstorm, issue, define, design.epic, design.story, plan), because validateBodyAndCitations is shared by all of them, and into the step prompts that author callSites or pathsCited.

migration.backwardCompat: An artifact already on disk is neither rewritten nor re-validated: the check runs only when a stage synthesizes a new artifact. The record shapes are unchanged (call sites and refs remain strings), so every reader and renderer of an existing record keeps working. A new synthesize that previously passed with a prose-bearing call site or ref now fails once and is re-emitted.

alternativesConsidered.name: Rule in prompts and schema descriptions only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Define the path rule once in scope-prompts.ts and put it in the prompts and field descriptions that author path-valued fields; add no check.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add one shared constant (beside ANTI_OVERREACH_RULE) that states the form: a project file is written relative to the project root with an optional :line, never shortened and never with prose in the same span; an external file is written with its full path. Interpolate it into every synthesize prompt in src/workflow/orchestrator.ts (each of which emits citations) and into the step prompts that author callSites and pathsCited, and add a description to those schema fields that points at the same wording. Nothing rejects a bad path, so a model that ignores the rule is not caught.
pros: Smallest change: one constant, a few interpolation sites and schema descriptions
Follows the existing pattern for shared prompt fragments, so the wording cannot drift
Fixes the cause the issue names: nothing tells the stages how to write a path
cons: Nothing catches a bad path, so a lapse is found only when someone clicks it
Depends on the model following prompt text
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Fixes the stated cause with the smallest change, but leaves nothing to catch a lapse, and the issue asks to consider a write-time check.

alternativesConsidered.name: Rule plus a shape check at write time
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: a1, plus a check in the artifact validation that rejects a path-valued field that is not a bare root-relative or absolute path.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Do a1, and add a check beside the citation check in src/workflow/synthesizer.ts that reads the path fields the artifact carries (an LLD's callSites, and the ref of a citation of kind code or doc) and fails with kind 'paths' and the offending entries in details. pathsCited is a step output, not part of the artifact, so it gets the schema description only and is not checked at write time. A project path passes when it is a bare path, optionally with a line form the chat page already links (:N, :N-M or :N:C), that does not start with ./ or contain .. or spaces or prose; an external path passes when it is absolute. The check looks only at the string, never at the disk, so it is deterministic and needs no repo access. The failure goes through the existing retry loop, so the model is told which entries to fix.
pros: A bad path is caught when the artifact is written and corrected by the existing re-emit
Catches the two seen defects: prose in the span, and a form that is not a path
No disk access: the same result in tests and in the daemon
cons: A shortened path such as artifacts/plan.ts still passes the shape check, because only the disk can say it does not resolve
Adds a new failure kind to the validation result and to its callers

alternativesConsidered.name: Rule plus a check that the path resolves from the root
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: a2, and the check also requires every project path to exist under meta.repoPath.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Do a2, and in addition resolve each project-relative entry against the artifact's meta.repoPath and fail an entry that does not exist there. This is the only form that catches a shortened path. It also fails a path to a file the story is about to create (a planned new file in callSites or a plan task), so it needs an allowance for new files, and it makes validation depend on the state of the working tree at write time.
pros: Catches the shortened path, the defect the issue names first
Matches the issue's wording: flag a path that does not resolve from the root
cons: A file the story creates does not exist yet, so the check must tell a planned file from a wrong one, which it cannot do from the string
Validation now depends on the working tree, so the same artifact can pass in one checkout and fail in another
Largest change and the most likely to reject good artifacts
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Catches the shortened path but cannot tell a planned new file from a wrong one from the string, and makes validation depend on the working tree. It risks rejecting good artifacts, so it is the wrong trade for a bugfix.
